summary: Created a local CA "OS Comparison Root CA" on node1 (Ubuntu 16.04) and installed it as a trusted system CA. Key generated with openssl genrsa 4096, self-signed x509 cert built with a compatible config file (openssl 1.0.2 lacks -addext), copied to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and activated via update-ca-certificates, which produced the PEM plus subject-hash symlinks in /etc/ssl/certs. Verified openssl trusts it by default (no -CAfile override needed). Completed mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline and CA health, rebooted node1 via `shutdown -r now`, confirmed connection refused during the outage window, polled until SSH returned, verified boot_id changed, and re-verified CA trust (checksum, symlink, openssl verify, subject/dates) all matched post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/tooling (Ubuntu 16.04.7, openssl, update-ca-certificates, sudo -n)
Generated 4096-bit RSA CA private key at /etc/ssl/os-comparison-ca/os-comparison-root-ca.key
Wrote openssl config with v3_ca extensions (basicConstraints=CA:TRUE, keyUsage=keyCertSign,cRLSign) since openssl 1.0.2 lacks -addext
Generated self-signed x509 CA certificate CN=OS Comparison Root CA valid 10 years
Installed cert into /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and ran update-ca-certificates
Verified cert present in /etc/ssl/certs as PEM with correct subject-hash symlinks (3c558648.0, 567518df.0)
Verified openssl trusts the cert using the default system trust store (no -CAfile override)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and CA health baseline
Rebooted node1 with sudo shutdown -r now, returning acknowledgement before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirming connection-refused during outage
Confirmed boot_id changed post-restart, proving an actual reboot occurred
Re-verified CA cert integrity (checksum), symlink, and openssl verify success after restart
